title: Tensor/sheafification comparison in the pro-etale site universes
statement: Let C be a category with objects in Type (u+1) and morphisms in Type u, J a Grothendieck topology, O a presheaf of commutative rings in Type (u+1), and R a sheaf of such rings. Assume abelian-group sheafification in this coefficient universe and its locally bijective criterion. Let alpha:O -> R be locally injective and locally surjective. Let a_alpha be module sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] and use the intrinsic sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There is a natural isomorphism a_alpha(F) tensor_R a_alpha(G) -> a_alpha(F tensor_O G), characterized by its inverse sending the sheafification of f tensor g to the tensor of the two sheafification units, with the canonical tensorObjIsoSheafification identification. This is the canonical tensor comparison, simultaneously natural in F and G.

proof.text: Construct the sheaf tensor universal property directly from the sectionwise tensor universal property and the module sheafification adjunction. A restriction-compatible bilinear family gives a presheaf tensor morphism, which factors uniquely through sheafification. Pure tensors and the adjunction prove uniqueness.

Tensor the two sheafification units sectionwise; their semilinearity makes this balanced over O. Sheafify the resulting morphism and use tensorObjIsoSheafification to obtain c:a_alpha(F tensor G) -> a_alpha(F) tensor a_alpha(G), with the displayed pure-tensor formula.

Extend the original pure-tensor pairing uniquely across both module sheafification units by the declared bilinear extension theorem. The universal property from step 1 gives a morphism in the opposite direction.

Check both inverse identities after precomposition with the units and on pure tensors. Sheafification uniqueness and uniqueness of bilinear extension prove equality. The same argument proves naturality in both variables. For the final tensorObjIsoSheafification naturality calculation use the inverse counit naturality and the monoidal tensorator naturality, without unfolding the localized monoidal structure.

theorem exists_sheafificationTensorIso_proEtaleUniverses
    (α : (O ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1}) ⟶
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj R).obj)
    [Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective J α] [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J α] :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    ∃ e : (sheafification α).prod (sheafification α) ⋙ tensor _ ≅
        tensor (PresheafOfModules.{u + 1}
          (O ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})) ⋙
          sheafification α,
      ∀ (F G : PresheafOfModules.{u + 1} (O ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1}))
        (U : Cᵒᵖ) (f : F.obj U) (g : G.obj U),
        (e.inv.app (F, G)).val.app U
          (((sheafificationAdjunction α).unit.app (F ⊗ G)).app U
            (f ⊗ₜ[O.obj U] g)) =
        (SheafOfModules.tensorObjIsoSheafification
          ((sheafification α).obj F) ((sheafification α).obj G)).inv.val.app U
            (((sheafificationAdjunction
              (𝟙 ((sheafCompose J
                (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj R).obj)).unit.app
              (((sheafification α).obj F).val ⊗ ((sheafification α).obj G).val)).app U
                ((((sheafificationAdjunction α).unit.app F).app U f) ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj U]
                  (((sheafificationAdjunction α).unit.app G).app U g)))
